100: HTTP 100 Continue — headers received, go ahead and send the request body
101: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols — server is switching protocols as asked (usually starting a WebSocket)
201: HTTP 201 Created — request succeeded and a new resource was created (typical POST/PUT result)
202: HTTP 202 Accepted — request received but processing is not finished yet (async job)
203: HTTP 203 Non-Authoritative Information — success, but a proxy modified the response
204: HTTP 204 No Content — success with no body to return (typical DELETE result)
205: HTTP 205 Reset Content — success; the client should reset its form or view
206: HTTP 206 Partial Content — only the requested Range was sent (resumed downloads, video streaming)
301: HTTP 301 Moved Permanently — the address moved for good; use the new one in the Location header
302: HTTP 302 Found — temporarily redirected to another address
303: HTTP 303 See Other — fetch the result from another address with GET (after a form submit)
304: HTTP 304 Not Modified — your cached copy is still current; use it
307: HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect — temporary move; unlike 302, keeps the method and body
308: HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect — permanent move; unlike 301, keeps the method and body
400: HTTP 400 Bad Request — malformed request (missing parameter, invalid JSON, etc.)
401: HTTP 401 Unauthorized — authentication required; not logged in, or the token is missing or expired
402: HTTP 402 Payment Required — payment needed (rarely used; some APIs use it for exceeded plan limits)
403: HTTP 403 Forbidden — authenticated but not allowed; logging in again will not help
404: HTTP 404 Not Found — nothing at this address; typo in the URL, deleted, or the path changed
405: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed — this address does not support the method (e.g. POST sent where only GET works)
406: HTTP 406 Not Acceptable — cannot respond in any format listed in the Accept header
407: HTTP 407 Proxy Authentication Required — the proxy needs authentication (common on corporate networks)
408: HTTP 408 Request Timeout — the client took too long to send the request, so the server closed the connection
409: HTTP 409 Conflict — clashes with the current state (concurrent edit, creating something that already exists)
410: HTTP 410 Gone — permanently deleted; unlike 404, it will not come back
411: HTTP 411 Length Required — a Content-Length header is required
412: HTTP 412 Precondition Failed — a condition header like If-Match did not hold (someone else changed it meanwhile)
413: HTTP 413 Content Too Large — request body too big (upload size limit exceeded)
414: HTTP 414 URI Too Long — URL too long (oversized query string; send it with POST instead)
415: HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type — the server does not accept this body format (check Content-Type)
416: HTTP 416 Range Not Satisfiable — requested range is outside the file size
417: HTTP 417 Expectation Failed — the server cannot meet the Expect header
421: HTTP 421 Misdirected Request — sent to a server that cannot handle it (HTTP/2 connection reuse issue)
422: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Content — well-formed but invalid content (validation failed)
426: HTTP 426 Upgrade Required — switch to another protocol (e.g. TLS or a newer HTTP version)
428: HTTP 428 Precondition Required — a condition header like If-Match is required to prevent lost updates
429: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests — rate limited; wait for Retry-After before retrying
431: HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large — headers too big (often too many cookies piled up)
451: HTTP 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons — blocked for legal reasons
500: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error — something broke on the server side; check the server logs
501: HTTP 501 Not Implemented — the server does not implement this feature (method) at all
502: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway — the gateway/proxy got a bad response from the upstream server (often the upstream is down)
503: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable — the server temporarily cannot take requests (overloaded, maintenance)
504: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout — the gateway/proxy timed out waiting for the upstream server
505: HTTP 505 HTTP Version Not Supported — the server does not support the HTTP version of the request
EPERM: errno EPERM — operation not permitted — the caller lacks the privilege, not the file permission
ENOENT: errno ENOENT — no such file or directory
EINTR: errno EINTR — interrupted by a signal; retry the call
EIO: errno EIO — I/O error from the device or filesystem
E2BIG: errno E2BIG — argument list too long
ENOEXEC: errno ENOEXEC — not an executable format
EBADF: errno EBADF — bad file descriptor — closed, or never opened for this mode
ECHILD: errno ECHILD — no child processes to wait for
EAGAIN: errno EAGAIN — resource temporarily unavailable; on a non-blocking socket this just means no data yet
EFAULT: errno EFAULT — bad address — a pointer the kernel cannot read
EBUSY: errno EBUSY — device or resource busy
EXDEV: errno EXDEV — cross-device link — rename across filesystems needs a copy
ENFILE: errno ENFILE — too many open files on the system
EMFILE: errno EMFILE — too many open files in this process — usually a descriptor leak
ENOTTY: errno ENOTTY — not a terminal — an ioctl the device does not support
ENOSPC: errno ENOSPC — no space left on device
ESPIPE: errno ESPIPE — illegal seek — the target is a pipe or socket
EPIPE: errno EPIPE — broken pipe — the other end closed the connection
ERANGE: errno ERANGE — result out of range
ENAMETOOLONG: errno ENAMETOOLONG — file name too long
ELOOP: errno ELOOP — too many symbolic links — a link cycle
ENOSYS: errno ENOSYS — function not implemented on this system
EADDRINUSE: errno EADDRINUSE — address already in use — another process holds the port
EADDRNOTAVAIL: errno EADDRNOTAVAIL — cannot assign the requested address
ECONNREFUSED: errno ECONNREFUSED — connection refused — nothing is listening on that port
ECONNRESET: errno ECONNRESET — connection reset by peer
ECONNABORTED: errno ECONNABORTED — connection aborted by the local side
EHOSTUNREACH: errno EHOSTUNREACH — no route to the host
EMSGSIZE: errno EMSGSIZE — message too long for the socket
EINPROGRESS: errno EINPROGRESS — operation now in progress — normal for a non-blocking connect
EALREADY: errno EALREADY — operation already in progress
